Today's Featured Research Reports

Shares of NVIDIA have underperformed the Zacks Semiconductor - General industry over the past year (-31.1% vs. -25.8%). Nevertheless, the company continues to benefit from broad demand for accelerated computing as customers build AI factories across hyperscalers, AI clouds, enterprises and sovereign buyers. Blackwell Ultra supports growth while Vera Rubin expands the platform across GPUs, CPUs, networking and software. 

Broader adoption, more content per system and usage-linked opportunities extend the growth runway, while cash generation supports substantial capital returns. The buildout also increases exposure to long-term supply commitments, extended customer payment terms and contingent guarantees. 

China remains constrained by export controls, while concentrated customer relationships, a costlier product ramp and competition can weigh on margins and cash flow. The founder's departure adds succession risk as NVIDIA moves to scale its next generation of systems.

(You can read the full research report on NVIDIA here >>>)

Cisco's shares have outperformed the Zacks Computer - Networking industry over the past year (+21% vs. +20.5%). The company's outlook benefits from a broad networking upgrade cycle, rising hyperscaler AI spending and deeper silicon and optics integration. New design wins and a large campus refresh opportunity support sustained demand. 

Security adoption and AI-led operations broaden the growth base, while tighter cost control adds operating leverage. Cash generation continues to fund shareholder returns. However, the shift toward hardware and higher memory costs are weighing on gross margins. Services growth remains modest, while competitive product cycles require disciplined execution. 

Acquisitions add integration exposure, and the stock's premium valuation leaves limited room for setbacks. The breadth of networking demand, rising AI revenue expectations and earnings leverage outweigh these risks, supporting the Outperform recommendation.

(You can read the full research report on Cisco here >>>)

Shares of BHP have outperformed the Zacks Mining - Miscellaneous industry over the past year (+32.3% vs. -0.1%). The company's low-cost iron ore franchise, growing copper earnings contribution and copper and potash projects support its long-term cash generation. Technology and the BHP Operating System continue to lift productivity, while fiscal 2026 cash flow and capital recycling provide funding flexibility. 

Record iron ore volumes and premium steelmaking coal exposure reinforce these strengths. Lower copper grades and processing variability constrain output before expansion projects contribute. Higher unit-cost guidance, heavy investment and Jansen capital escalation increase execution demands. 

Softer iron ore pricing and a less favorable Chinese pig iron outlook limit earnings visibility. Suspended nickel assets and Samarco's continuing cash obligations add portfolio and financial risks as BHP advances its organic growth program.

(You can read the full research report on BHP here >>>)

GEE's shares have underperformed the Zacks Staffing Firms industry over the past year (-6.3% vs. +47%). This microcap company with a market capitalization of $19.30 million is witnessing its contract staffing remains under pressure amid cautious hiring and labor-market uncertainty, while Hornet Staffing's failure to meet acquisition performance thresholds raises execution concerns. Cash generation also remains uneven. The shares trade near their historical median valuation. 

Nevertheless, GEE Group's return to profitability despite lower revenues reflects benefits from a richer direct-hire mix, cost reductions and productivity initiatives. Higher-margin direct-hire placements and improved contract staffing margins have strengthened overall profitability, while a leaner expense base could provide operating leverage when hiring demand recovers. 

Technology investments, including AI-enabled recruiting and integrated operating platforms, may further improve efficiency and scalability. The exit from industrial staffing has also sharpened the company's focus on professional staffing and higher-margin opportunities. 

(You can read the full research report on GEE here >>>)

Shares of Tandy Leather Factory have outperformed the Zacks Retail - Apparel and Shoes industry over the past year (+10% vs. +1.1%). This microcap company with a market capitalization of $18.02 million has seen third-quarter 2026 sales rose 7.3% to $18.5 million, while operating income rebounded to $0.6 million from a year-earlier loss. Pricing initiatives, sales campaigns and better product allocation support profitability. 

Tandy Leather Factory's 102-store network, specialist service, e-commerce reach and commercial offerings provide growth avenues, while a new loyalty program may encourage repeat purchases. A renewed $5 million buyback authorization adds flexibility, with no credit-facility borrowings reported. 

However, tariff refunds drove much of the quarterly margin gain, while a prior-year distribution shutdown eased comparisons. Cash fell to $5.7 million, inventory reached $37.5 million and nine-month operating cash outflow totaled $2.8 million. Higher occupancy costs and tariff uncertainty temper the improved outlook.

(You can read the full research report on Tandy Leather Factory here >>>)

Spotify Technology reported a third quarter that exceeded its own guidance, with Premium and ad-supported operations supporting higher revenue, wider gross margin, and strong operating income, while management reaffirmed a long term operating margin target above 20% by 2030.

The business is preparing a paid AI remix and cover service for early 2027, which would add another way to monetize its large user base and content library, alongside expanding audiobooks and creator tools.

The focus now turns to how Spotify's margin expansion story could be affected by its AI remix plans and recent conference commentary.

Spotify Technology Investment Narrative Recap

To own Spotify Technology, you need to feel comfortable with a simple idea. The platform keeps adding users while trying to widen profitability through better unit economics across Premium, ads, audiobooks, and future AI features. According to IamPotato, an investor in the Simply Wall St Community, the key debate is how durable that margin progress will be as content and product spend evolve.

The latest conference remarks and recent ETF net buying streak do not radically change the near term story. The main catalyst still sits in execution on operating margin, including the path toward the above 20% 2030 goal. The biggest risk remains content costs, including higher minimums for labels, which could squeeze that margin if pricing or mix shifts disappoint.

The planned paid AI remix and cover service for early 2027 is the announcement that matters most for this setup. It directly relates to Spotify Technology's effort to add new, potentially higher margin revenue on top of an existing user base, alongside audiobooks and creator tools that IamPotato highlights as important for monetization depth.

This feature also sits next to higher per subscriber minimums at partners such as Warner Music Group, which represent a cost headwind. Execution on AI remix pricing, rights structures, and user adoption becomes an operational catalyst. Weak take up or heavier royalty terms could slow the margin expansion that management and many investors are watching closely.

On IamPotato's numbers, the fair value of Spotify Technology lands at $714.13. This figure is based on a 12.0% annual revenue growth path and a future profit margin of 15.7%, which together outline what the business could earn once scale and operating discipline settle in.

Spotify Technology has delivered a powerful 217.6% gain over the past three years, yet its recent flat year to date move and softer short term returns put the focus squarely on whether the current share price aligns with the cash the company can generate over time. With the stock now trading around US$577, the key issue is how much of Spotify's future cash flows are already embedded in that valuation.

A 217.6% rise over three years means anyone looking at Spotify today is really asking how durable its long term cash generation story could be from here.

Management's goal of lifting operating margins over the coming years, including a long term aim above 20% by 2030, can meaningfully shift expectations for future free cash flow and therefore what investors might rationally pay today.

If you are weighing Spotify's 217.6% three year run against the cash flow expectations now baked into US$577, it can help to line it up beside 40 high quality undervalued stocks.

Is Spotify Technology Fairly Priced on Cash Flow?

The Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) approach here looks at what Spotify Technology might return to shareholders in cash over time, then pulls those figures back to today. Spotify generated about €3.21b of free cash flow over the last twelve months, and the model assumes that this cash base keeps growing rather than shrinking, with projected free cash flow rising into the next decade.

Those rising cash projections help explain why a share price of US$577.03 can still line up with what the DCF model implies, even without assuming extreme expansion. The recent news around management aiming for an operating margin above 20% by 2030, following a solid quarter and product plans like an AI remix add on, supports the idea that higher profitability is embedded in these cash flow estimates and already reflected in the current valuation. SPOT

Cathie Wood Just Sold $5 Million of Spotify © Africa images via Canva
Key Takeaways

Cathie Wood's ARK Invest sold 8,961 shares of Spotify from one ETF on Friday, worth about $5.2 million at Friday's close.

Analysts expect Spotify's normalized EPS to nearly double from 2025 to 2028, and the stock trades below its average forward P/E since 2024.

Warner Music Group's subscription streaming growth sped up to 15% on higher per-subscriber minimums, and those minimums are a cost for Spotify.

The numbers don't back the sale, so I'd hold, and Spotify's early-February report is the next test.

Cathie Wood's ARK Invest sold 8,961 shares of Spotify (SPOT:NYSE) on Friday, according to ARK's daily trade email. At Friday's close of $577.03, that's about $5.2 million.

The sale came a day after Warner Music Group (WMG:NASDAQ), one of the biggest labels Spotify licenses music from, reported a quarter that shows how much the labels are getting out of streaming's price rises. What's good for Warner is a cost for Spotify.

One ETF, and a sliver of it

All 8,961 shares came out of the ARK Next Generation Internet ETF (ARKW), and ARK's email puts them at 0.14% of the ETF. The $5.2 million is worked out as shares times Friday's close, because the email doesn't say what ARK got for them. The email also lists only the portfolio adjustments ARK's team made that day, so it may leave some trades out.

ARK manages about $17.4 billion. Its 13F for the quarter ended Sept. 30, filed Nov. 13, lists 181 US stock positions. A day's email doesn't say why ARK sold or how much Spotify it still holds. What it does show is a small sale from one fund.

TIKR tracks 41 analysts on Spotify. How many say "Buy"?

See the full breakdown of Buy, Hold, and Sell ratings on Spotify, along with Wall Street's revenue and earnings estimates, all in one place. More than 500,000 investors use TIKR to research stocks like this one. See Spotify's Analyst Ratings

The earnings keep climbing

Analysts expect Spotify's normalized EPS to rise every year through 2028:

Spotify Technology (SPOT): normalized EPS, actual and consensus estimates, $ per share, fiscal 2023-2028 (TIKR)

That's growth of about 13% in 2026, 28% in 2027 and 26% in 2028, which takes EPS close to double 2025's level. The 2026 increase looks small because Spotify paid almost no tax on its 2025 earnings, helped by a deferred tax benefit. Analysts expect an effective tax rate of about 22% this year.

The business underneath is still heading the right way. Third-quarter revenue rose 16% to €4.97 billion and gross margin reached 33.0%. Management guides fourth-quarter operating income to €820 million, up 17% from a year earlier.

Spotify also isn't priced like a company growing this fast. At 37x forward earnings, it trades below the roughly 48x it averaged at quarter-ends from March 2024 through September 2026, and not far above its 31x low in June 2026.

Key Takeaways

Spotify stock is up 12.5% in the past month as the Nasdaq 100 fell, on a third quarter that beat guidance.

Warner Music Group, still negotiating over Spotify's planned AI remix add-on, is sharing in streaming price increases.

CFO Christian Luiga reaffirmed a 20%-plus operating margin target for 2030, against 12.8% in 2025.

Spotify trades below its usual multiple, a buy if the fourth quarter delivers 10 million net adds and a 16% operating margin.

Spotify Technology (SPOT:NYSE) stock is up 12.5% in the past month on a strong quarter and a planned AI add-on. Meanwhile, the Nasdaq 100 fell 10%.

On Nov. 19, CFO Christian Luiga told Morgan Stanley's conference that Spotify still aims for an operating margin above 20% by 2030. The same day, record label Warner Music Group (WMG:NASDAQ) reported faster streaming growth.

TIKR tracks 41 analysts on Spotify. How many say "Buy"?

See the full breakdown of Buy, Hold, and Sell ratings on Spotify, along with Wall Street's revenue and earnings estimates, all in one place. More than 500,000 investors use TIKR to research stocks like this one. See Spotify's Analyst Ratings

Price did the heavy lifting

Spotify added 6 million Premium subscribers in the third quarter, 1 million above guidance. Premium revenue grew 17%, nearly twice as fast as subscribers, and gross margin hit a third-quarter record of 33.0%.

Operating expenses rose 26%, though, holding the operating margin to 13.5%. Co-CEO Alex Norström said Spotify's "costs are moderating, and there is more runway ahead." Its fourth-quarter guide of €820 million of operating income, a 15.8% margin, also topped Wall Street's estimate.

Analysts expect normalized EPS to rise about 45% from 2025 to 2027:

Spotify Technology (SPOT): normalized EPS, actual and consensus estimates, $ per share, fiscal 2024-2029 (TIKR)
AI gives subscribers something new to pay for

Premium revenue per user grew 7.5% at constant currency in the third quarter. Management guides 4.5% to 5% for the fourth quarter as Spotify laps price increases in more than 150 markets.

On Oct. 30, the Financial Times reported that Spotify plans a paid AI remix and cover service for early 2027. It could cost $4 to $5 a month extra. Universal Music Group has reportedly signed, but Sony Music and Warner haven't.

Warner has leverage. Its recorded-music subscription streaming growth sped up to 15% last quarter. Warner credits that partly to higher per-subscriber minimums from streaming services. It also lists AI licensing among its drivers for fiscal 2027. Whether it signs, and at what royalty, decides how much of that $4 to $5 Spotify keeps.

title: Warner Music: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors
detail:
Warner Music: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors
The Motley Fool Team, The Motley Fool
Thu, November 19, 2026 at 2:07 PM EST 3 min read
SPOT
WMG
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

On its fourth-quarter 2026 earnings call, held on Nov. 19, 2026, Warner Music (NASDAQ:WMG) reported an all-time high annual revenue, driven by accelerating subscription streaming. Contractual price increases with streaming partners and expanding operational margins show the music publisher is turning structural industry shifts into durable cash flows. Discipline in talent investments and new digital licensing models position it well for multiyear expansion. Three things management said stand out.

1. Contractual Price Increases Fuel Streaming Acceleration

Warner Music negotiates per-subscriber minimum (PSM) rate floors with major digital service provider (DSP) platforms, such as Spotify and Apple Music, to ensure a guaranteed baseline price. These contractual uplifts drove subscription streaming revenue up 15% in the fourth quarter.

In Q4, total revenue increased 7%, led by an acceleration in Recorded Music subscription streaming growth to 15%. This performance was bolstered by the successful implementation of contractual PSM increases across several of our major DSP partners and continued market share gains in most of our major operating regions.
-- Robert Kyncl, CEO

2. Cost Discipline Drives Margin Expansion Past Targets

Operating efficiency initiatives helped Warner Music widen its full-year adjusted operating income before depreciation and amortization (OIBDA, a metric of core operational profit) margin by 210 basis points, surpassing its annual guidance target. Transforming operations from a traditional holding structure into a technology-driven operating business provides lasting leverage.

The expansion is really driven by several items, our strategic reorganization and the ongoing cost management efforts, including the savings we've realized from the restructuring plan, which will continue into '27.
-- Louis Dickler, acting CFO

3. Generative AI Partnerships Unlock New Royalty Streams

Rather than resisting generative artificial intelligence (AI) tools, Warner Music is pioneering licensing frameworks that capture royalties when AI services use its catalog. Securing commercial agreements with creation platforms establishes a key monetization model as user interactivity expands across digital channels.

As a result of our partnership, in September, following the launch of its latest model, Suno became the first of what will be many generative AI companies paying revenue to rights holders.
-- Robert Kyncl, CEO

Looking Ahead

Operational leverage and guaranteed minimum pricing models provide Warner Music with a predictable foundation for growth. Digital subscription renewals, catalog investments, and artificial intelligence licensing will drive cash conversion.
